// scope: This is a FLAT, all-14-blocks-included smoke run of sonic_top at the smallest parameter point every SYNTH_PARAMETERS knob supports -- N_TILES=1 (not the shipping 4), T=8 (not 64), ROUTER_LANES=4/SEGS=8 (the exact recipe that finished the standalone sonic_router run, see ../router/config.json and p4/RESULTS.md), CONV_CH=4, LMHEAD_K=4, SEQ_DEPTH=32, N_SRAM_BANKS=1, SRAM_AW=6 (64 words/bank). HANDOFF.md's T4.2 is explicit that the shipping-scale chip (TILE=64, 4 tiles, full 32-expert/64-lane router, 16x512KB SRAM) will NOT go through a flat LibreLane run -- the real path is hierarchical (harden tile/router/sram_bank once each, instance as macros via MACROS+MACRO_PLACEMENT_CFG). This config's only goal is to prove the FULL RTL HIERARCHY -- all 18 files, all 12 real digital blocks sonic_top instantiates -- makes it through synthesis-to-GDS as one netlist at all, the same 'flow-qualification, reduced scale' posture already proven for sonic_router (225k cells, 4h40m, clean DRC/LVS/antenna) and sonic_tile/sonic_sram_bank (T4.1 in HANDOFF.md). Do not quote any timing/power/area number from this run as a shipping-scale or 14nm claim.
// phy: sonic_phy_lpddr5x.sv is included in VERILOG_FILES (it's part of the design) but sonic_top.sv does not instantiate it -- this is intentional, not a wiring gap. It models a commercial hardened LPDDR5X PHY macro (DFI 5.0), which in a real chip never goes through digital std-cell synthesis; it is dropped in as a hardened macro at the very top, outside this flow, same reason sonic_ioring's PLL is a behavioral stub rather than synthesized analog. p4/README.md's caveat #3 already says there is no open Sky130 LPDDR5X PHY to instantiate here. Leaving the file in VERILOG_FILES is harmless (Yosys will just not elaborate an uninstantiated module) and keeps this config's file list matching sonic_top.sv's header comment 1:1 for anyone diffing the two.
// clock: 1500 ns reuses the router's own proven-working number verbatim (p4/RESULTS.md: WNS/TNS=0, DRC/LVS/antenna clean at LANES=4/SEGS=8/1500ns) rather than guessing tighter for a first combined run neither this repo nor LibreLane has attempted before. sonic_tile (T4.1) and sonic_sram_bank both closed cleanly at 1000ns standalone, so 1500 should be conservative headroom for the union. Tighten after this run reports real post-CTS slack, exactly as router's config-next.json (800ns) tightened after the segs8 run measured 567ns worst path.
// util: 35%/40% is BELOW every existing block config (router 40/45, tile 65/68, sram/seq 45) on purpose: this is the first-ever combination of all 12 blocks in one netlist, so the resulting cell mix and congestion hot spots (top-k network + weight plane + descriptor ring all in one flat design) are unmeasured. HANDOFF.md's T4.1 log shows BOTH tile and sram_bank failed global placement (GPL-0301) or detailed placement post-CTS (DPL-0036) on their first two attempts before landing on ~40-45% -- start lower here, tighten only after a clean run establishes real headroom.
// macros: No MACROS / MACRO_PLACEMENT_CFG key here on purpose. There are no hardened macros in this run -- SRAM banks and the router's PWL table synthesize to flip-flops (Finding 25 in p2/README.md), same as every other block run so far. The macro_placement.cfg file in this directory is a sketch for the FUTURE hierarchical T4.2 run (pre-hardened tile/router/sram_bank instanced as real macros) and does not match this flat run's instance names -- do not point MACRO_PLACEMENT_CFG at it here, it will fail to resolve instances.
// keys: LibreLane errors on unrecognised config keys. Only keys beginning with // are exempt, which is why the comments look like this.
